A closure can add dynamic advice - the advice is activated/deactivated with the closure.Relative advice is relative to the closure.

The memberName is the name of a member to get from the requested capability.When a requirement is resolved an ICapability is returned - this is the capability that is the provider of the requested capability (not always the same as the actual thing being required) - the user of the capability must know how to access what the capability consists of (if it consists of something tangible).For a requirement to be included in the prerequisites the following conditions apply:- The contributor flag of the IRequirement must be true- The requirement must be resolved- The partName must reference a property of the returned capability, if blank, "self" is assumed.- The resolution for the required capability must return an ICapability that returns an interface derived from IGenericUnit.
If not empty, specifies a list of parts which requirements should be considered when resolving. If empty, all parts are considered.

If not empty, specifies a list of parts which requirements should be excluded when resolving. If empty, no exclusion takes place.If a part is mentioned in both includeParts and excludeParts, the exclusion has precedence.
Prunes the resulting build unit to only include the parts specified with include and exclude parts.

A Resolver is reponsible for resolving a request for a build unit.As an attempt to resolve can be time consuming (or simply not wanted) all resolvers have the possibility to filter out requests (this also means that it is possible to avoid activation of unused bundles just to be informed that the resolver should not be used).

An EFS based resolver presents a (read only) EFS interface to the root of a component.Clients should expect that directories may not be browseable.It is the responsabiity of an implementation to translate the combination of the location string and request information (name, namespace, version, etc) into anEFS {@link org.eclipse.core.filesystem.FileStore}.

Gets the connector by looking up the connectorType in the Runtime (getConnectorFor(connectorType)).This connecor can be cached for subsequent resolutions.Evaluates the location using the current IPropertyScope => useLocationCreates an instance that implements TranslationRequest (has reference to IConnector, and possibly IQuery, and IRequest)Obtains an IMetaDataTranslator from the Runtime MetaDataTranslatorFactory using the TranslationRequest.Calls resolve on the IMetaDataTranslator with the TranslantionRequest as argument.TranslationRequest implements IAdaptable.The IMetaDataTranslator adapts the TranslationRequest to the Accessor interface it is interested in - e.g. EFSBasedAccess.Specializations of MetaDataTranslators can thus implement new interfaces and classes that b3 has no knowledge of.
Obtained from Runtime IMetaDataTranslatorFactory to suit the particular Resolver.

This resolver uses the current active workspace, and can thus use EFS to access all material in the workspace (resource: URI). The workspace resolver thus benefits from EFS mapping of artifacts external to the workspace location.If the location is empty, the workspace resolver assumes resource:/{b3.bu.name} to be the EFS URI.If the location is a path, it is assumed to be a resource path.TODO: If a scheme is used (other than resource) - what should happen - if a workspace layout "on disk" is being appointed for instance - it would need to interpret workspace meta data to understand mapped parts in that workspace's virtual filesystem (complex).
This resolver interprets the location as either a path or an EFS URI - i.e. it can point to anything "mounted" in the EFS filesystem.If a path is used - a file: scheme is used.

A BuildUnit command represents an invocation of a b3 command. Such a command acts on build units (one or several), and these are described with an IUnitRequest.An action could resolve and import the build units, another could invoke an action on a particular build unit.The Command is executed with some additional information:- a reference to a resolver determines from which "repositories/resolvers" the requet should be satisfied. This makes it possible to to describe and invokation of an action on a build unit that is not yet present in the local environment (provided it can be found in the IResolver used). A different configuration could use the default IResolver that only looks in the workspace and target platform, etc.When a command is executed, it can also define a set of properties, and advice to be applied to instances in the build model being constructed.Such advice is provided by an IPointCut.
A selector of nodes in the IBuildContext. Probably based on XPath. This selector defines what the advice is applied to in the IBuildContext.
Advices on a filter. The filterOp controls if the advice should replace the current value, or be combined using AND or OR.
Makes nestede advice relative to the featurePath of the group.

A pattern filter simpler than a full regexp. This class is useful to capture patterns without having to express them as regular expressions.(i.e. if someone wants to translate ANT or Shell scripts into this model).
